question: Paano ang proseso ng full retirement ng business permit at magkano ang multa kung lumampas ng 30 days bago mag-file?
answer:
The process for the full retirement of a business permit involves the following steps:

1. Gather the required documents, which include the latest business permit (either original or certified copy), an affidavit of full retirement for single proprietorships, and a partnership resolution for partnerships (if applicable). These documents should be notarized by any Notary Public. [S2, S3]

2. Submit the recommended and approved application for retirement and receive a claim stub. [S4]

3. The Processing Staff of the Business Bureau processes the claim and releases the retired business permit and other required documents. [S1]

4. If the application is filed more than 30 days after cessation, a late filing fee of P1,000 to P5,000 will be imposed. [S1]

For more detailed information, you may refer to the Business Bureau's Citizen Charter 2026_VOL.I & II.pdf.

ground_truth: For Full Retirement of a Business Permit upon cessation of operations, applicants must submit: 1) Latest original Business Permit or certified copy; 2) Notarized Affidavit of Full Retirement stating the reason and exact effective date of retirement (Single Proprietorship), or Partnership/Board Resolution; 3) Valid ID and SPA if represented; and 4) Physical surrender of the Business Identification Plate. Late filing fees range from PHP 1,000.00 to PHP 5,000.00 if the retirement application is submitted more than 30 days from actual business cessation, in addition to gross sales tax obligations assessed by the CTO.
